body:
OpenAI just announced it is "Advancing computer use with Ironclad."

Computer use means the AI can click through a screen for you, not just answer in a chat box. It fills forms, moves between tabs, finishes a task end to end.

Everyone will write about what Ironclad does. Here is what it means for a freelancer running ads with no team behind them.

Right now, most "automation" in a small ad account is you, at 11pm, copying a lead from a Meta notification into a spreadsheet. Computer use tools are built to do exactly that step — the boring click between two screens that nobody automated because it was too small to bother with.

That is also the exact gap that loses money today. Across nine Meta ad accounts I've run, nothing captured what happened after a lead came in. No reorder timing, no follow-up, a "not interested" treated as final — and some of those leads came back on their own, months later, and ordered.

A tool that can click through screens doesn't fix a strategy problem. It fixes a nobody-got-around-to-it problem. Those are most of what actually breaks in a small business.

Open your own lead form today. Where does a submission land — your inbox, a sheet, nowhere? What's the last manual step between a lead coming in and someone actually calling them?
